definition.description: REV | Scoring | Calculate & Flag. Score (FR-011, max 60), inverted life-satisfaction (FR-012), Likert points (FR-013), status thresholds (FR-014), income flag (FR-015). Never reads rev_narrativeraw or other special-category data (FR-016). See notes.md.

metadata.description: Environment variable. Recipient of the FR-019 Borderline routing message and the FR-022 incomplete-answers message (C-TECH-047).

Environment variable. Base URL of the REV Grant Administration app up to and including appid; the card buttons append pagetype, etn and id. May be empty - the card says so and the HTML fallback drops to plain text (C-TECH-047).

When_an_application_is_created.description: Row CREATED on rev_application only, not modified - a modified trigger would re-score on every edit and fight the override guard. Runs as the flow owner so it can log errors even when the process owner creates the row by hand. See notes.md.

Stop_if_the_process_owner_has_overridden.description: FR-018 short-circuit, deliberately the FIRST action: a human's decision outranks the automation, so the flow exits before reading configuration or computing anything. Exists so the flow stays safe to re-run by hand (TAD 5.2). See notes.md.

Initialise_failure_detail.description: Holds the failed action name and reason for the alert. Declared at the TOP level: the scope that fails is skipped from the failure onward, so nothing inside it can carry a value out.

Score_and_flag.description: One scope so one failure branch catches everything below it.

Read_configuration.description: Every number this flow decides with comes from a rev_setting row read at RUN TIME by alternate key - nothing bound at import, nothing literal (FR-017, NFR-019). The board changes a threshold by editing a row. See notes.md.

Read_scoring_configuration.description: FR-011/013/015. ONE List rows call for all 8 rev_setting rows. Was 8 chained Get-a-row-by-id calls whose Row ID held an alternate-key expression, which the connector rejects - the flow failed before its first write. See notes.md.

parameters.$filter: rev_name eq 'LikertPointMap' or rev_name eq 'FeelingScaleInversion' or rev_name eq 'KnockoutThreshold' or rev_name eq 'BorderlineBandLower' or rev_name eq 'BorderlineBandUpper' or rev_name eq 'IncomeCeiling' or rev_name eq 'IncomeBandUpperBoundMap' or rev_name eq 'MaxCircumstanceScore'

Fail_if_a_setting_row_is_missing.description: A missing rev_setting row was a 404 under Get-a-row-by-id; under List rows it is a short array and first() would return null, scoring everyone wrongly rather than failing. All 8 rows are required. See notes.md.

Stop_run_configuration_incomplete.description: Fails the run so REV | Ops | Failure Alert records it. Scoring on a partial configuration would produce a plausible wrong number, which is worse than no number at all.

runError.message: Expected 8 rev_setting rows and found @{length(body('Read_scoring_configuration')?['value'])}. Run provisioning/dataverse/seed-settings.ps1 for this environment. No score was calculated.

Setting_LikertPointMap.description: FR-013. Maps each rev_likertresponse value to points. Value 1 ('None of the time') scores 5, value 5 ('All of the time') scores 1 - the score measures need, not wellbeing. Labels corrected in 0.3; mapping unchanged. See notes.md.

Setting_FeelingScaleInversion.description: FR-012. Inversion is a lookup map, not arithmetic, so a scale change is configuration only. Since 0.3: eleven entries keyed 0-10. Expresses 10 minus the raw answer per the Solution Design. See notes.md.

Setting_KnockoutThreshold.description: FR-014, FR-020. Awaiting SDD OQ-001; prd-settings.json deliberately holds a {{PENDING_OQ_001}} token so seed-settings.ps1 refuses to seed production with an unconfirmed criterion.

Setting_IncomeBandUpperBoundMap.description: Maps each rev_incomeband value to the top of that band, compared against the configured ceiling. A field mapping the process owner controls (NFR-019). Sentinel -1 means 'not stated' -> income flag 3. See notes.md.

Setting_MaxCircumstanceScore.description: Used only to render the score breakdown as 'n out of 60'. Read from configuration rather than written as 60 in the text, so the breakdown cannot describe a maximum the scoring no longer has.

Collect_wellbeing_answers.description: THE TEN Likert answers paired with question number - ten, not eleven (corrected in the schema revision; column 95 is the separate life-satisfaction answer). Lets the breakdown name each answer. See notes.md.

Find_missing_wellbeing_answers.description: 'Missing' now means missing OR UNUSABLE, widened in 0.8 (test D-014, TC-317): an answer present but not a key of LikertPointMap used to pass this gate and throw downstream. Check is 'is it a map key', not a hardcoded range (FR-017). See notes.md.

Withhold_the_outcome_when_a_scored_answe.description: FR-022/NFR-018: incomplete data must not produce a spurious rejection, so the application goes to Under Review with NO score written. Widened in 0.8 to 'absent OR unusable' on all eleven scored answers (test D-014). See notes.md.

List_the_missing_question_numbers.description: Projects the missing wellbeing answers to their question numbers. A Select ACTION, not a select() expression: there is no such expression function, and item() is only valid inside an action like this one. See notes.md.

parameters.item/rev_scorebreakdown: @{concat('NO AUTOMATED OUTCOME - a scored answer was missing or could not be scored (FR-022).', decodeUriComponent('%0A%0A'), 'Wellbeing answers that were absent, or held a value the current scoring configuration has no point value for: ', if(greater(length(body('Find_missing_wellbeing_answers')), 0), join(body('List_the_missing_question_numbers'), ', '), 'none'), decodeUriComponent('%0A'), 'Life-satisfaction answer supplied: ', if(empty(coalesce(string(triggerOutputs()?['body/rev_feelingscaleanswer']), '')), 'no', 'yes'), decodeUriComponent('%0A'), 'Life-satisfaction answer scoreable: ', if(empty(coalesce(string(outputs('Parse_feeling_scale_inversion')?[string(triggerOutputs()?['body/rev_feelingscaleanswer'])]), '')), concat('NO - the value supplied is not one the current scoring configuration recognises. Check it against the 0 to 10 scale.'), 'yes'), decodeUriComponent('%0A%0A'), 'Status set to Under Review. No circumstance score has been calculated and none should be inferred. Complete the missing answers with the applicant and re-run scoring, or set the status by hand and record the override reason.')}

Tell_the_process_owner_an_answer_is_miss.description: NFR-018 requires 100% of these to reach a human, so this is pushed. Adaptive card: a facts panel naming what was missing, and buttons to this application and the Under Review queue. HTML fallback behind it (IMP-0125). See notes.md.

Tell_the_process_owner_an_answer_is_miss.description: Fallback for the card above: the same facts as HTML with anchors instead of buttons, so a rejected card payload still reaches the process owner. Reference and question numbers only - no name, condition or narrative.

parameters.body/messageBody:
Application needs review - a scored answer was missing

  • Reference: @{triggerOutputs()?['body/rev_name']}
  • Status: Under Review
  • Circumstance score: not calculated
  • Wellbeing answers missing: @{if(greater(length(body('Find_missing_wellbeing_answers')), 0), join(body('List_the_missing_question_numbers'), ', '), 'none')}
  • Life-satisfaction answer: @{if(empty(coalesce(string(outputs('Parse_feeling_scale_inversion')?[string(triggerOutputs()?['body/rev_feelingscaleanswer'])]), '')), 'missing, or not a value the scoring configuration recognises', 'supplied')}

@{if(empty(parameters('rev_GrantAdminAppUrl')), 'Open Under Review - Incomplete Scoring in REV Grant Administration.', concat('Open this application, or the Under Review queue.'))}

Complete the missing answers with the applicant and re-run scoring, or set the status by hand and record your override reason. No score has been written, and none should be inferred.

Reference and question numbers only - no name, condition or narrative is included in this message by design.

Parse_likert_point_map.description: Moved ahead of the FR-022 completeness gate in 0.8: the gate now also checks each answer is a key of this map, so the map must be parsed first. Parse_feeling_scale_inversion still runs after the gate. See notes.md.

Parse_feeling_scale_inversion.description: Also moved ahead of the FR-022 gate in 0.8, for the same reason as Parse_likert_point_map: the life-satisfaction answer has the same unmappable-value exposure (test D-014 fact 6). See notes.md.

Initialise_likert_points.description: Float, not integer, since 0.8: 'Not sure' is worth 0.5 points (map key 6), so an odd count of 'Not sure' answers leaves a half point. An integer variable would truncate that half point. Rounded once, at the end. See notes.md.

Score_each_wellbeing_answer.description: FR-013/FR-011. Concurrency pinned to 1: this loop mutates shared variables, and Power Automate parallelises Apply to each by default - two parallel increments can read the same value and lose one. See notes.md.

Add_the_configured_points_for_this_answe.description: float(), not int(), since 0.8 - this cast was the mechanism of test D-014: int() threw on a non-whole map value (0.5, 'Not sure') and on any missed lookup. Missed lookups are now handled upstream. See notes.md.

Record_this_answer_in_the_breakdown.description: FR-035: names the question, response option and points, so the breakdown evidences the score to a trustee. Option VALUES not labels. One exception since 0.8: value 6 ('Not sure') is named explicitly. See notes.md.

inputs.name: breakdownLines
inputs.value: @{concat('Wellbeing answer ', string(item()?['question']), ': response ', string(item()?['response']), if(equals(string(item()?['response']), '6'), ' (Not sure)', ''), ' = ', string(outputs('Parse_likert_point_map')?[string(item()?['response'])]), ' points', decodeUriComponent('%0A'))}

Invert_the_feeling_scale_answer.description: FR-012: lower life satisfaction produces a higher score (need, not wellbeing). Scale is 0-10; contribution is 10 minus the raw answer (0.3), per the Solution Design. Inversion is a table lookup, not arithmetic. See notes.md.

Calculate_circumstance_score.description: FR-011: ten wellbeing answers at up to 5 points (50) plus the inverted life-satisfaction answer at up to 10 gives 0-60 - read from MaxCircumstanceScore, not a constant here. Confirmed at 60 in 0.3. See notes.md.

Round_the_circumstance_score.description: Rounds the (possibly fractional, since 'Not sure'=0.5pt) total HALF UP via formatNumber. FIXED in 0.9 (D-015): .NET's 'F0' rounds half TO EVEN, mis-rounding X.5 totals and skipping required review. The +0.25 offset forces half-up. See notes.md.

Resolve_income_band_upper_bound.description: -1 when the applicant chose not to state an income band, or when the band is not in the map at all. Either way the flow reports that it cannot assess rather than assuming.

Derive_income_flag.description: FR-015. Deliberately separate from the circumstance score: 1 within the ceiling, 2 above it, 3 not stated. An applicant above the income ceiling isn't silently penalised in their need score.

Derive_status.description: FR-014: 4 Auto-reject at/below knockout, 3 Borderline inside the band, 2 Auto-pass above it. Knockout checked FIRST. Evaluated against the ROUNDED score since 0.8 - must match what's stored. See notes.md.

Compose_score_breakdown.description: FR-011/FR-035. Trustee-visible evidence of how the score was reached: scored answers, points, totals and thresholds applied only - no narrative, condition data or identity. Records thresholds in force at scoring time.
Compose_score_breakdown.inputs: @{concat('Circumstance score: ', string(outputs('Round_the_circumstance_score')), ' out of ', string(first(body('Setting_MaxCircumstanceScore'))?['rev_value']), decodeUriComponent('%0A'), 'Scored on: ', formatDateTime(utcNow(), 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm'), ' UTC', decodeUriComponent('%0A%0A'), variables('breakdownLines'), 'Life-satisfaction answer ', string(triggerOutputs()?['body/rev_feelingscaleanswer']), ' out of 10, inverted = ', string(outputs('Invert_the_feeling_scale_answer')), ' points', decodeUriComponent('%0A'), 'Wellbeing subtotal = ', string(variables('likertPoints')), ' points', decodeUriComponent('%0A'), 'Exact total before rounding = ', string(outputs('Calculate_circumstance_score')), decodeUriComponent('%0A'), if(equals(outputs('Calculate_circumstance_score'), outputs('Round_the_circumstance_score')), 'No rounding was applied - the total was already a whole number.', concat('Rounded to ', string(outputs('Round_the_circumstance_score')), '. A half point arises when an odd number of answers is "Not sure", which is worth 0.5 points; halves are rounded UP, in the applicant''s favour, because a higher score means greater need.')), decodeUriComponent('%0A%0A'), 'Thresholds in force at the time of scoring:', decodeUriComponent('%0A'), '  knockout at or below ', string(first(body('Setting_KnockoutThreshold'))?['rev_value']), decodeUriComponent('%0A'), '  borderline band ', string(first(body('Setting_BorderlineBandLower'))?['rev_value']), ' to ', string(first(body('Setting_BorderlineBandUpper'))?['rev_value']), decodeUriComponent('%0A'), '  income ceiling ', string(first(body('Setting_IncomeCeiling'))?['rev_value']), decodeUriComponent('%0A%0A'), 'Special-category data was not read by the scoring calculation (FR-016).')}

Write_score_and_status.description: One write, at the end, once everything is computed - a failure part-way through leaves the application unscored rather than half-scored. FR-020: writing status 4 removes it from the Active Applications view.

Route_borderline_applications_to_the_pro.description: FR-019/NFR-018: 100% of Borderline outcomes need human judgement before they progress. Carries reference, score and income flag - not the applicant's name.

Notify_borderline_card.description: FR-019/NFR-018. Adaptive card: a facts panel, and buttons straight to this application and to the Borderline queue. The HTML message behind it runs if this fails, so the routing message still arrives (IMP-0125). See notes.md.

Notify_borderline.description: Fallback for the card above: the same facts as HTML with anchors instead of buttons, so a rejected card payload still routes the Borderline outcome to a human. Anchors are guarded on rev_GrantAdminAppUrl. See notes.md.

parameters.body/messageBody:
Borderline application - needs your judgement

  • Reference: @{triggerOutputs()?['body/rev_name']}
  • Circumstance score: @{outputs('Round_the_circumstance_score')} of @{first(body('Setting_MaxCircumstanceScore'))?['rev_value']}
  • Borderline band: @{first(body('Setting_BorderlineBandLower'))?['rev_value']} to @{first(body('Setting_BorderlineBandUpper'))?['rev_value']}
  • Income: @{if(equals(outputs('Derive_income_flag'), 1), 'Within the ceiling', if(equals(outputs('Derive_income_flag'), 2), 'Above the ceiling', 'Not stated'))}

This application will not progress until you review it.

@{if(empty(parameters('rev_GrantAdminAppUrl')), 'Open Borderline - Awaiting Review in REV Grant Administration.', concat('Open this application, or the Borderline queue.'))}

If you disagree with the score, change the status and record your reason - the override is kept against your name.

Reference, score and income flag only - no name, condition or narrative is included in this message by design.

Find_the_failed_action.description: The child of the failed scope whose status is Failed. result(scope)[0] was used before and returns the FIRST child, whose message on a nested scope is a generic wrapper - 11 alerts once said only "An action failed".

Describe_the_failure.description: When the failed child is the nested Read_configuration scope, descend one level to the action that actually failed. Otherwise the outer child IS the leaf.

Find_the_failed_step_inside_Read_configu.description: Only evaluated when Read_configuration is the failure, so result() on it is safe.

Set_failure_detail_from_the_nested_scope.description: The leaf action inside the nested scope - the one with the real message.

inputs.name: failureDetail
inputs.value: @{concat('Action: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_step_inside_Read_configuration'))?['name'], 'unknown'), ' | Code: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_step_inside_Read_configuration'))?['error']?['code'], 'none'), ' | Reason: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_step_inside_Read_configuration'))?['error']?['message'], 'no message supplied by the platform'))}

Set_failure_detail.description: The failed child was not a scope, so it is already the leaf.

inputs.name: failureDetail
inputs.value: @{concat('Action: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_action'))?['name'], 'unknown'), ' | Code: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_action'))?['error']?['code'], 'none'), ' | Reason: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_action'))?['error']?['message'], 'no message supplied by the platform'))}

Compose_run_link.description: Builds the deep link to THIS run and passes it to REV | Ops | Failure Alert. Both parts come from workflow() at run time, so nothing is hardcoded. It must be built here: workflow() in the child returns the child. See notes.md.

Alert_on_failure.description: FR-010. Passes the application REFERENCE, never the row. A scoring failure leaves the application at status Submitted with no score - the safe resting state (NFR-018 fail-closed).
